outlook.statement: To carry on the business of generating, developing, establishing, operating and maintaining solar power plants and other renewable energy projects; to generate, produce, and supply electricity from solar energy; and to transmit, distribute, supply, and sell such electricity to electricity boards, utilities, or private/public entities, intermediaries in Power Transmission/Distribution, Companies, Industrial Units, or to all types of users/consumers of Energy and to trade, deal in, import, export, install, repair, maintain, and service all kinds of solar energy systems, equipment, devices, and components.

To carry on the business of consultants, advisors, auctioneers for all type of solar energy/renewal energy plants and to undertake research and development in the field of solar energy and other allied fields.

To acquire concessions or licenses granted by or to enter into contracts with, the Government of India, any State Government, Municipal, Local Authority or other Statutory bodies, Companies or any other person for the development, erection, installation, establishment, construction, operation and maintenance of Solar Power Plants and in this regard to promote, develop, own, acquire, set up, erect, build, install, commission, construct, establish, maintain, improve, manage, operate, alter, control, take on hire/lease, carry out and run all necessary Plants, equipment, sub-stations, workshops, generators, machinery, transmission facilities, electrical equipment, accumulators, repair shops, wires, cables, lamps, fittings and apparatus in the capacity of principals, contractors, developers or otherwise and to deal, buy, sell and hire/lease all apparatus and things required for or used in connection with generation, distribution, supply, accumulation of Solar/renewal Energy.

Textile industry facing challenging period due to prevailing Geo-Political situation, strained relations among several countries, global slowdown and weak demand. Expected recovery of economies and domestic demand coupled with Government initiatives to benefit textile industry in coming years. Anticipation of revival of global economy over medium term, textile scenario would change and demand for Company's products likely to pick up.

The industry outlook for FY27 remains uncertain, with growth drivers intact but near-term performance constrained by demand uncertainty, input cost volatility and geopolitical disruptions. A broad-based recovery will depend on revival in global consumption and export markets.
India's textile and apparel market is projected to reach US$ 350 billion by 2030, supported by rising domestic demand, growing exports, and policy interventions strengthening competitiveness.

The sugar industry is entering a new phase accelerating ethanol production, positioning itself at the centre of India's renewable energy transition, with significant scope to meet increasing demand for ethanol, strengthening both energy security and farmer incomes.

Global slowdown in economies
Weak demand of textile products
Waning demand because of weak environment and prevailing global scenario
Non-viable operations of spinning unit (Arham Spinning Mills) leading to closure
The Company has laid down a Risk Management Policy and identified threat of such events which if occurs will adversely affect the ability of the company to achieve its objectives.

The Company is in the business of Yarns, Fabrics and Sugar. The Company has not dealt in any commodity market and thus there is no commodity price risk. To cover itself from exchange rate fluctuations with respect to export of its products, the company does partial hedging by normal booking in the normal course of the business. The Company is not involved in any speculative activities.
Fluctuating raw material costs (cotton, sugarcane)
Geopolitical supply chain disruptions (West Asia conflict, Red Sea shipping disruptions, Russia-Ukraine war)
Intense competition from low-cost hubs (Bangladesh, Vietnam, China)
Fragmented manufacturing base
Tightening global sustainability requirements and labour/forced labour scrutiny
Depreciation of Indian rupee
Rising protectionist measures and trade restrictions
Climate instability and erratic yields affecting cotton and sugarcane
High crude oil prices elevating input and logistics costs
Sugar industry: mismatch between sugar prices and sugarcane costs (FRP vs MSP)
Shrinking sugar surplus limiting export opportunities
Government export limits on sugar prioritizing domestic food security
Heavy reliance on monsoon rainfall
Groundwater depletion in key sugarcane cultivating states
Short crushing seasons, outdated mill machinery, labour-intensive harvesting
Regulatory and policy shifts affecting operations and long-term planning
Market risk comprising interest rate risk, currency risk and other price risks
Credit risk from operating activities (primarily trade receivables) and financing activities
Liquidity risk - risk of shortage of funds
Interest rate risk on long term debt obligations with floating interest rates
Foreign currency risk on trade payables denominated in foreign currency
Impact of new labour codes (four labour codes consolidated from 29 existing legislations)
Interest rate risk on variable rate borrowings
Foreign currency risk on unhedged trade payables in USD, EUR, CHF
Impact of new labour codes (four labour codes) on employee benefits expenses
